# CR-007 — Quote model + outcome attribution / ใบเสนอราคาและการผูกผลลัพธ์

**Status:** approved (Boss, 2026-08-09) · **Mode:** DDD
**Plan ref:** SmartGift `docs/implementation-plan-2026-08-09.md` §5 (ZUMP01 Phase 3) · **Design ref:** `smart-crm-design-2026-08-08.md` §6 (rule A6 — attribution before analytics)

## Problem / ปัญหา

SmartGift's historical data contains **5,540 quotations with no recorded outcome**. Nobody can say
what fraction was won, lost on price, or simply never answered — so close rate, pipeline value and
sales forecasting are all unanswerable from the data that exists. That is not a reporting gap that
better dashboards can fix later; it is an **attribution gap baked in at the moment each quote was
created**, and no amount of analysis recovers it.

Zuri today has `Order` and `Invoice` but **no quote at all**. Every quote SmartGift issues from now
on must carry its customer and its outcome from the first second, or the same hole re-opens.
ใบเสนอราคาย้อนหลัง 5,540 ใบไม่มีผลลัพธ์บันทึกไว้เลย — วิเคราะห์ย้อนหลังไม่ได้ ต้องผูก customer + outcome ตั้งแต่วันแรก

## Decisions that shape this CR / การตัดสินใจ

**1. `customerId` is NOT nullable.** This is the entire lesson of the 5,540. A quote that cannot
name its customer cannot be attributed, so the schema refuses to store one. (`Invoice.customerId`
is nullable for walk-in POS sales — a quote has no walk-in case.)

**2. Two fields, one state machine.** `status` is the document's lifecycle
(`DRAFT | SENT | CLOSED`); `outcome` is the commercial result
(`open | won | lost_rejected | lost_no_response`). They are not independent: the **invariant
`outcome !== 'open'` ⇒ `status === 'CLOSED'`** is enforced in one repository transition function so
the two can never drift apart, and a quote still `DRAFT` may not carry an outcome at all.

**3. Aging is a fact, not a guess.** A quote sent 90 days ago with no answer is recorded as
`lost_no_response` with `agedAt` stamped, so "we never heard back" is distinguishable in the data
from "they said no" (`lost_rejected`). Both are losses; only one is a pricing signal.

## Change / การแก้

| # | Piece | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Prisma model `Quote`** | `id` uuid · `quoteNo String @map("quote_no")` (QUO-YYYYMMDD-NNN, **unique per tenant** via `@@unique([tenantId, quoteNo])` — not a global unique, since the daily-serial generator scans each tenant's own rows and two tenants legitimately produce the same serial on the same day) · `tenantId` · **`customerId String` (NOT NULL)** · `conversationId String?` (the LINE thread it came from, `onDelete: SetNull`) · `amount Decimal @db.Decimal(12,2) @default(0)` · `status String @default("DRAFT")` · `outcome String @default("open")` · `issuedAt DateTime?` (set when it becomes `SENT`) · `respondedAt DateTime?` · `agedAt DateTime?` · `notes String? @db.Text` · `createdById String?` (Employee) · `createdAt`/`updatedAt`. Relations to Tenant/Customer/Conversation with explicit `onDelete` (house convention, FEAT-033). Indexes: `@@unique([tenantId, quoteNo])`, `@@index([tenantId, status])`, `@@index([tenantId, outcome])`, `@@index([tenantId, issuedAt])` — the aging scan and the future close-rate query both read on these. |
| 2 | **Migration** | Hand-written additive migration `prisma/migrations/<ts>_quote_attribution/migration.sql` creating one new table (no change to existing tables beyond the FK), following the style of the most recent migration in that directory. Nothing to backfill. |
| 3 | **`src/lib/repositories/quoteRepo.js`** (new) | `create(tenantId, { customerId, conversationId, amount, notes, createdById })` — generates `quoteNo` via `generateQuoteNo()` (`idGenerator.js`'s `generateDailyId('quote','quoteNo','QUO')`, scanned per-tenant), rejects a missing/foreign `customerId` and a non-finite/negative `amount`, retries **once** on P2002 (generation is read-then-write and a single tenant can issue quotes in bursts; the unique constraint itself is `[tenantId, quoteNo]`, not global — see piece 1). `send(tenantId, id)` → `status=SENT`, stamps `issuedAt`, **only from `DRAFT`** (rejects a replay against an already-SENT/CLOSED quote, which would otherwise re-stamp `issuedAt` and reset the aging clock). **`setOutcome(tenantId, id, outcome, { respondedAt, agedAt })`** — the single transition function that enforces decision 2's invariant, refuses an unknown outcome, refuses reopening a `CLOSED` quote back to `open`, and refuses `agedAt` paired with any outcome other than `lost_no_response` (AC4 enforced here, not by caller discipline). `listByCustomer`, `listByTenant({ status, outcome, limit, cursor })`, `findById`, and `listAgingCandidates({ tenantId?, issuedBefore, take })` (worker read path — API routes cannot import Prisma directly). Every query tenant-scoped. |
| 4 | **Aging worker** — `src/app/api/workers/quote-aging/route.js` (new) | Mirrors `workers/cert-nightly/route.js` shape: `verifyQStashSignature`, `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`, `maxDuration = 55`, optional `{ tenantId }` in the body for a targeted run. Reads candidates via `quoteRepo.listAgingCandidates` (`status='SENT'`, `outcome='open'`, `agedAt=null`, `issuedAt <= now - 90d`) — never a direct Prisma import, per the repo-pattern ESLint guardrail; sets `outcome='lost_no_response'`, `agedAt=now`, `status='CLOSED'` through `setOutcome` (never a raw update, so the invariant holds). **Idempotent** — a second run the same day finds nothing because `agedAt` is set. Returns `{ aged: n, tenantIds: [...] }` and logs the count. Batch-capped (e.g. 500/run) with the remainder left for the next run; the cap must be **logged**, never silent. |
| 5 | **API** — `src/app/api/quotes/` | `POST /api/quotes` (create, `{ domain:'customers', action:'W' }`) · `GET /api/quotes?customerId=&status=&outcome=` (list) · `PATCH /api/quotes/[id]` — accepts only `{ action: 'send' }` or `{ outcome, respondedAt? }`; any other key → 400. All routes go through `quoteRepo` (no `getPrisma` — repo-pattern guardrail), resolve the customer/quote within the caller's tenant, `404` outside it. `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`. |
| 6 | **UI** | A **Quotes** section on the customer detail surface (`src/app/(dashboard)/crm/[id]/page.jsx`, alongside the CR-006 business panel): list of that customer's quotes (no., amount, status, outcome, issued date), a create form, and per-quote actions to mark `won` / `lost_rejected`. Thai-first labels (ใบเสนอราคา / ยอดเงิน / สถานะ / ผลลัพธ์ / วันที่เสนอ). When the page is opened from a conversation context, pass `conversationId` through on create; a richer inbox-side flow is out of scope. |
| 7 | **Tests** | `quoteRepo`: create rejects missing/foreign customer, P2002 retry path, `setOutcome` enforces the invariant (open⇒SENT allowed, won⇒CLOSED forced, unknown outcome rejected, outcome on a DRAFT rejected), all queries tenant-scoped. Aging worker: ages exactly the quotes past 90 days, leaves fresh/answered/already-aged ones alone, is idempotent across two runs, honours the batch cap and logs it, and **401s without a valid QStash signature**. Routes: create/list/patch happy paths, unknown key → 400, cross-tenant → 404. |

## Acceptance Criteria / เกณฑ์ยอมรับ

- **AC1** A quote cannot be created without a customer in the caller's tenant (schema + repo +
  route all refuse); every quote row therefore has attribution from creation.
- **AC2** `setOutcome` is the only way an outcome changes, and after it `outcome !== 'open'` always
  implies `status === 'CLOSED'`. An outcome on a `DRAFT` quote is rejected.
- **AC3** The aging worker converts a 91-day-old unanswered `SENT` quote to
  `lost_no_response` + `agedAt`, leaves an 89-day-old one untouched, and a second run changes
  nothing (idempotent).
- **AC4** `lost_no_response` and `lost_rejected` are distinguishable in the data — the aging worker
  never writes `lost_rejected`, and a human decision never writes `agedAt`.
- **AC5** Unsigned requests to the worker return 401.
- **AC6** `npm run lint` + targeted vitest + `npm run test:scripts` green; `npx prisma validate` passes.

## ⚠️ Deploy prerequisite found during recon — affects all 24 workers, not just this one

`src/lib/qstash.js` reads **`QSTASH_TOKEN` / `QSTASH_CURRENT_SIGNING_KEY` / `QSTASH_NEXT_SIGNING_KEY`**,
but the QStash instance provisioned in CR-004 injected its variables into Vercel with a **`ZURI_QSTASH_*`
prefix**. Until those names are reconciled (either re-map in Vercel or read both names in
`qstash.js`), **every QStash-signed worker fails signature verification and returns 401** — the
aging worker included. This CR does not change `qstash.js` (that is a platform-wide change deserving
its own CR), but the aging job will not run in production until it is resolved. Recorded here so it
is not discovered as "the worker silently never ran".

The QStash **schedule** itself must also be created (console or API) pointing at
`POST /api/workers/quote-aging`, daily — the repo's only `vercel.json` cron is `health-check`, so
scheduling here follows the existing QStash convention rather than adding a Vercel cron.

## Out of scope / นอกขอบเขต

- **Importing the 5,540 historical quotations — forbidden.** They are customer PII under the
  design doc's `local_only` rule and stay in the local DuckDB SoT; historical close rate reaches
  Zuri only as an aggregate through the CR-008 snapshot path. This CR is about quotes issued
  **from now on**.
- Close-rate / pipeline-value reporting and dashboard tiles (CR-010) — this CR only makes the data
  exist and be trustworthy.
- Automatic customer **stage** transition when a quote is sent or won: that needs the per-tenant
  pipeline presets from CR-005, which is not on `main` yet. Deliberately deferred so this CR stays
  independently mergeable; follow-up once CR-005 lands.
- Quote PDF/document generation, line items (amount is a single total for now), approval workflow,
  quote→order conversion, and the `QUOTE_AGED` automation trigger (CR-009).

## Rollout / การปล่อย

One new table, no change to existing data → additive migration, safe on a live database. Nothing
reads quotes until staff create them, so deploy is behaviour-neutral. The aging worker does nothing
until its QStash schedule exists **and** the env-name issue above is resolved.
